title: Prove exact optimal circular Schur bandwidth (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped all-size proof with finite corroboration: after one nonempty proper arc is eliminated from a full negative circular band of radius w, the exact minimum Schur half-bandwidth over simultaneous row/column permutations is `min(M-1,2w)`, where M is the survivor count. Arbitrary band-supported coefficients with an invertible arc pivot retain the same upper bound.

```text
surviving path: 0, 1, ..., M-1
new order:     0, M-1, 1, M-2, ...
upper bound = minimum-degree lower bound = min(M-1, 2w)
```

At M=9, w=2, the inherited linear survivor order has bandwidth eight; the new order has four, and no order has three. This answers the ordering question in James Reed / jwr404's merged #4289, following #4286. Their no-cancellation argument is a credited premise. This contribution is produced by Nick Petalas. No predecessor executable is imported or replayed.

## Evidence

- Before: #4289 determines circular-distance fill and explicitly leaves survivor reordering open.
- After: `PROOF.md` identifies the path-power-plus-end-clique support, constructs an order and proves a matching degree lower bound. The all-size result rests on this argument.
- Exact finite corroboration passes on 4,656 graph/radius pairs through M=96, all 362,879 vertex permutations for 36 pairs through M=8, and 651 circular graph-elimination layouts through n=16. Nine invalid-input rejections and four semantic controls pass.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized registered checks pass locally on CPython 3.12.15 / macOS 27.0.1 arm64, taking 1.65 and 1.66 seconds in direct timed runs. Generated receipts agree and bind all six package files by SHA256.
- Committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export integrity and a read-only Git-free optimized replay pass. The exported files remain unchanged. A read-only proof/code review found no mathematical blocker; independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

From the repository root, use these exact local reproduction commands; substitute an installed Python 3.12 path on another machine:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/cycle-schur-optimal-order
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/cycle-schur-optimal-order/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/cycle-schur-optimal-order/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/cycle-schur-optimal-order --check-source-history
```

Expected scientific marker: `PASS_CYCLE_SCHUR_OPTIMAL_ORDER`. Standard library only. Direct verification is self-contained; generic provenance checks require the pinned Git history. Verification writes no files unless an external new receipt path is explicitly supplied.

## Limitations

Exactness uses H=I-E with every in-band off-diagonal E entry positive, all others zero, and row sums below one. Signed or missing couplings retain the upper bound but can have a smaller optimum. Multiple eliminated arcs, the physical cost of permutations and all right-hand-side movement/restoration, inverse norms, rounded arithmetic, tape layout, compiler/hosting and a complete paid caller remain outside the claim. No physical supplier, new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. The selected 0.00302015 is unchanged. Full selected cold replay, proof-assistant checking and native Linux execution were not run.

## Open next questions

1. Bind the folded order and its inverse to one literal circular Gaussian boundary solve, retaining all right-hand sides and restoration, then price the complete movement. No physical conversion is provided here.
2. Specify a multiple-arc separation rule, derive its support graph, and decide whether its optimal bandwidth remains O(w). The one-arc theorem does not decide merged components.

## Related open work

No other open PR studying this one-arc optimal-order quantity was found in current targeted `bandwidth`, `Schur bandwidth` and `circular arc` title/body searches. Cached overlap coverage also included 395 open PRs and 3,889 Discussion records, with sparse local-note omissions. This is search coverage, not proof of novelty.

Merged #4373 by unpaidmoon and #4407 by Ryanson Jonathan concern linear separated carves and the different `2w-1` constant. Their results are cited without a new replay. Cinna Davis's #4100 supplies the Gaussian-boundary motivation.

The completion refresh read this account's nine other open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-22 22:40:40 UTC: #4873, #4874, #4875, #4876, #4878, #4880, #4881, #4882 and #4883. None studies the one-arc Schur support graph, its optimal linear half-bandwidth or a competing value of min(M-1,2w). No extra predecessor computations were run. #4880 studies Euclidean conditioning of unitary observation cycles, a different matrix family and quantity, so there is no shared numerical result to compare.

No full selected cold replay or extra native-platform campaign was run.

## Merge danger

Reversible. The change adds only `research/cycle-schur-optimal-order/`; shared code and selected-frontier files are unchanged.
